verdict.rationale: Aider has its own headless one-shot mode (`--message` runs one instruction, applies edits, then exits) and a Python scripting API. Its `--watch-files` mode keeps a background watcher running that acts on AI comments in your files. These are one-off or trigger-on-comment actions, not autonomous recurring automations: any scheduling would come from the user's external tools (e.g. cron), and the autonomy 'navigator-mode' is a community add-on, not an Aider feature. missing for 10: built-in recurring or scheduled background automations, autonomous multi-step background runs without per-task user prompts, first-party docs on running Aider as a background service.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Aider takes a `--message` argument, where you can give it a natural language instruction. It will do that one thing, apply the edits to the files and then exit.
If you run aider with `--watch-files`, it will watch all files in your repo and look for any AI coding instructions you add using your favorite IDE or text editor.
You can configure aider to run your test suite after each time the AI edits your code using the --test-cmd <test-command> and --auto-test switch.
